title: Claude Mythos slashed software work to onboard AMD GPUs to around three days
lede: Anthropic told IPO investors that Claude Mythos Preview handled bringing one model up on AMD MI355X GPUs in about three days, work it says once took six to twelve months.

points: A slide footnote limits the three days to prompt processing (prefill) for one model at a useful level of performance.
Co-founder Tom Brown says Mythos ported or wrote nearly all the kernels with almost no human intervention.
Anthropic has not said whether decode was covered, or how fast the model runs on AMD compared with Nvidia.
Tom's Hardware reads it as CUDA's software moat narrowing, though agents still need scarce GPUs to test the kernels they write.
Anthropic already runs on Nvidia and AMD GPUs, Google TPUs and AWS Trainium as one pooled fleet.

points.text: The main thread asks whether AI-written kernels erase CUDA's developer ecosystem, widely seen as Nvidia's real moat.
Several object that models able to do this work are withheld from the public and from AMD, so only the labs benefit.
One commenter doubts the claim's timing, landing just before Anthropic's IPO, and suspects hidden limitations.
Commenters expect the same speedup in any domain that is easy to verify, which shifts the problem to verifying harder ones.
